questions.question: Which parameter of main commonly contains the number of command-line arguments?
Which parameter of main commonly provides the argument strings?
What is the type of argv in the conventional declaration int main(int argc, char *argv[])?
options: B. Array of pointers to char

questions.question: What does argv[0] conventionally contain?
options: A. The first user-supplied option after the program name
B. The program name or invocation string

questions.question: If a program is invoked with no additional user-supplied arguments, what is argc conventionally at least?
What does argv[1] refer to when argc is greater than 1?
options: B. The first command-line argument after the program name

questions.question: Which declaration is a standard form of main for receiving command-line arguments?
What should a program check before accessing argv[2]?
options: A. That argc is greater than 2
D. That argv is an integer

questions.question: Are command-line arguments provided to a C program as strings?
options: B. No, they are always integers
C. No, they are always floats

questions.question: What is a common use of command-line arguments?
options: A. Passing configuration values or options when starting a program
